reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about dislocation-boundary interactions, an optimal grain size regime, and a transition to grain boundary sliding in tungsten at 800–1200 °C, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises.
premises: Grain boundaries in tungsten act as sinks/sources for dislocations, promoting dynamic recovery at high temperature.
An optimal fine grain size exists that enhances ductility and toughness relative to coarse-grained tungsten.
Excessive grain refinement leads to dominant grain boundary sliding, reducing toughness.
The proposed mechanism (dislocation absorption/emission at boundaries) is the primary mode of deformation in the optimal regime.
